savings.reason: Read with original section 4: discharge for completed compliant transfers, good-faith protection for historical conduct, and preservation of pre-transfer rights/debts/claims are accrued effects. EO:13350 section 1 saves prior acts, proceedings, matured rights/duties and incurred penalties. They do not continue new transfer instructions, fresh Treasury delegations, or an independent forward command under the revoked order.

research_rationale: The complete original creates Treasury and FRBNY transfer machinery for funds connected to UNSCR 778, with financial-institution directions conditioned on Treasury determinations. Its repayment contingencies and section 4 discharges are not a calendar sunset or proof of exhaustion. No earlier ending actor is indicated in the complete bounded search; EO:13350 expressly revokes EO:12817 and section 10 establishes July 30, 2004 at 12:01 a.m. EDT. Section 4 is expressly analyzed separately: discharge and good-faith immunity for transfers/conduct already undertaken, and pre-transfer claims, are accrued consequences preserved by EO:13350 section 1. Neither those savings nor the definitions and no-private-right language independently retain fresh transfer or holding authority after revocation. The inventory restores the missed section 2 and eliminates a heading-only section 8.
